content: Alchemical symbols, originally created as part of the early scientific discipline of alchemy, were utilized to represent certain elements and compounds up until the 18th century. While the notation was largely standardized, the specific style and symbols used could vary between individual alchemists. The symbols listed here represent the most commonly recognized forms. The so-called planetary metals were believed to be governed or influenced by one of the seven classical planets known to ancient civilizations. Although these metals occasionally had unique symbols of their own, they were more commonly represented by the symbols of their corresponding planets. The planets Uranus, Neptune, and the dwarf planet Pluto were discovered after the decline of alchemy and its replacement by modern chemistry. As a result, these celestial bodies are not associated with traditional alchemical symbols. However, some contemporary alchemists have assigned the symbols of these planets to represent the radioactive metals uranium, neptunium, and plutonium, respectively. The twelve core alchemical processes are regarded as the foundation of modern chemical processes. Each of these processes is believed to be governed or influenced by one of the twelve zodiac signs.
